A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OATH despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime benchmarks from locally simulated protocol execution, including logistic regression and feed-forward neural networks on five fairness datasets.

after.justification: v2 reports original Service and Audit runtime benchmarks on the same five datasets, including timing summaries across three trials in Table 1.

M1.justification: v1's initial fairness postprocessing and calibration-certification phase is removed, leaving Service and Audit phases. v2 Algorithms 1–2 introduce client-generated sensitive-attribute labels and checks on every query to prevent demographic reassignment. Appendix B also revises equalized-odds computation using authenticated ground-truth labels and label-conditioned counts. These change the procedure rather than merely its description.

E1.justification: Both versions use COMPAS, Crime, Default Credit, Adult, and German Credit with the same prediction tasks and demographic attributes. Neural-network scalability remains based on runtime estimates for the same network families. v2's distribution-shift discussion and schematic do not constitute an added empirical test scenario.

E2.justification: FairProof and the Mystique-based comparator remain in the neural-network comparison. However, v2 defines its baseline as per-query inference verification followed by group-fairness verification, whereas v1's Correctness Baseline includes inference verification alone. FairZK is newly discussed but is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The principal audit settings remain one million queries and 7,600 verified queries. Runtime accounting changes from v1's three-phase pipeline, including calibration certification, to v2's Service and Audit phases. v2 Figure 4(a) additionally evaluates estimated total runtime across query volumes. The conversion of audit timings from seconds to minutes is only a reporting change.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4(a) adds an analysis of neural-network total runtime versus query volume for OATH and its baseline. The component-runtime ablation, fairness-deviation envelope, evasion-probability curves, and five-dataset witness-count analysis already appear in v1 and are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 explicitly identifies its summaries as means and standard deviations across three trials and supplies uncertainty for FFNN audit runtimes. v1 reports unspecified plus/minus summaries for LR and point estimates for FFNN in Tables 2 and 6. This establishes improved disclosure, not an increase in the number of runs.

E6.justification: Initial-certification runtime results are removed, neural-network totals are revised, and query-volume scaling results are added. For 42.5M parameters, v1 Table 3 reports 9.98 million seconds for one million queries; v2 Figure 4(b) reports 4.43 seconds per query for the revised pipeline. These are not same-setting speedups. Most tabular audit means survive unit conversion, but Credit's LR mean changes from 5003.5 seconds to 83.3 minutes, and LR uncertainty values also change.

T1.justification: The detection bound is retained, but its justification changes materially. v1 Appendix 9 asserts that changing sensitive attributes does not invalidate the argument; v2 Appendix G instead relies on the new check preventing those changes. The revised proof also drops v1's explicit assertion that the argument covers all four fairness metrics. Calibration-certification guarantees are removed, and equalized odds receives a revised thresholded formalization and ground-truth-oracle assumption.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from end-to-end fairness certification spanning training, postprocessing, inference, and auditing to confidential online group-fairness certificates. v2 drops the initial model-certification guarantee and makes the distinction between offline and online certificates central to its abstract, introduction, and new conclusion. Efficient probabilistic auditing remains a core claim.

C2.justification: Appendices J–K add substantive qualifications that group fairness can coexist with inequitable treatment and should complement other auditing and human oversight. Appendix B explains when ground-truth labels might become available. v2 also introduces an inconsistent bottleneck interpretation: Section 5.1 names correctness checking, while Figure 2 and Appendix I.1 continue to identify consistency checking as dominant.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and dataset/toolkit licenses, but removes v1's M1 Pro chip specification, explicit FFNN layer configurations, and floating-point implementation discussion. Code availability is internally inconsistent: the introduction says it is public, while the checklist promises release upon acceptance. The PDFs establish changed disclosure, not verified repository availability.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially reorganized around offline versus online certification and distribution shift. v2 incorporates Holding Secrets Accountable, distinguishes OATH from concurrent FairZK through model flexibility, and explicitly connects its design to cut-and-choose cryptography. These revise the novelty argument beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and protocol narrative are extensively rewritten. Cryptographic background, comparisons, sampling details, and experimental explanations are reorganized across the main text and appendices. v2 also adds a conclusion, limitations, impact statement, and checklist, and updates authorship.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview schematic, merges LR and FFNN timing results into Table 1, and combines a redesigned neural-runtime table with new scaling plots in Figure 4. The approach-comparison table moves to Appendix A with different columns. Existing analytical plots are relocated and relabeled, including correction of the duplicated COMPAS label to Default Credit.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1's soundness reasoning through sensitive-attribute checks and improves equalized-odds computation and limitations. However, new protocol inconsistencies obscure the net improvement: v1's commitment and audit algorithms agree on field order, whereas v2 Algorithm 1 hashes q||alpha_s||o||r and Algorithm 2 checks q||alpha_s||r||o. Its retained Algorithm 7 also omits the safeguard used by the revised soundness proof. These unresolved specification problems affect core guarantees; the PDFs do not establish whether they are merely transcription errors.
